targetText: Turn and twist then as we may, the fact remains unaltered. If equivalents are exchanged, no surplus-value results, and if non-equivalents are exchanged, still no surplus-value. [18] Circulation, or the exchange of commodities, begets no value. [19]
explanation: Marx proves that trade alone cannot create net new value across society. If everyone buys low and sells high, gains and losses cancel out. Surplus value must therefore originate in production, not exchange.
